title: I Enforced the Fencing-Club Mask Checkout on the Coach Whose Nephew Skipped It

parts.text: I signed mask 7 at 5:40 p.m. and coach June's nephew was already in the piste with an unsigned bag. The log said: MASK ON THE SHEET. RETURN SANITIZED. NO GUESTS. I was thirty-one, adult beginner, holding a card that listed 7. June shrugged. "Family is atmosphere." I photographed the log, the unsigned bag, and the piste. Then I asked for the sanitation sheet. At 5:48 the armorer pinged why an unsigned mask was live. I did not argue the joke. I argued the file. A paper policy is only paper until someone treats it like a clock.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The armorer can see an unsigned mask live on the piste during my checkout.

social.video_title: The coach's nephew skipped the mask sheet — Part 1/2
social.description: Fencing club, an unsigned bag, a sanitation log. I asked for the sheet. Would you have photographed the piste?

parts.text: June called it a lesson until the armorer asked for the still. I printed the log, the bag, and the ping. The nephew sanitized and signed. June ran guests through the sheet like everyone else and told the next coach family was always about optics. Optics is a word coaches use when a log exists. Checkout now has a second line: NEPHEWS ARE GUESTS. I keep mask 7 on a labeled hook. June brown-bags her jokes. The piste finally looks like a sheet, not a family room. If it is written, it can be applied to the person who wrote it.

social.description: Sanitation sheet, a signed bag, and a second line. Was family ever the log?
